title: policy.yaml
description: Schema for policy.yaml, the sibling of personaxis.md inside .personaxis/[personas/<slug>/]. It holds operational policy over a persona: improvement_policy (how the persona may change), runtime constraints, evaluation suites and behavioral assertions. It is never placed in a model's prompt. The open engine reads improvement_policy.mode, which can only restrict the inline value in personaxis.md; `personaxis validate` checks the whole file, and the other blocks are declarations for a host or evaluator that implements them.

spec_version.description: Spec version the file was written for. policy.yaml has the same fields from 0.6.0 to 1.1.0, so any of those versions validates; 0.5.0 is accepted for backward compatibility.

applies_to.description: The personaxis.md this policy governs. persona_version_range lets several policy.yaml files cover different version ranges of the same persona.

persona_name.description: Must match the metadata.name of the personaxis.md in the same directory.

persona_version_range.description: Optional semver range (e.g. '>=1.0.0 <2.0.0'). When omitted, the policy applies to every version of the persona. Two policies for the same persona_name must not have overlapping ranges.

improvement_policy.description: Change governance: whether a change the persona proposes applies, waits for a person, or is refused. It can only restrict the inline improvement_policy of personaxis.md (the more conservative mode wins). 'locked' is the kill-switch: while it holds, nothing the persona proposes applies, its state included.

mode.description: locked: the kill-switch, for an incident or an audit. Nothing the persona or its model proposes applies, neither an edit to the spec nor a change to its state; only a person's own mutations and homeostasis (half_life) move it. It is the mode when none is declared. suggesting: the persona is alive. Changes to its state apply inside the declared envelopes and the drift thresholds; edits to the spec are proposed (propose_self_edit) and queued for a person. autonomous (high-risk): as suggesting, and spec edits also apply (apply_self_edit), each one a new PersonaVersion, bound by universal invariants, governance.per_layer_edit_policy, hard_limits and autonomous_scope_allowlist/blocklist; requires approved_by and last_approval_at. 'auto' is a deprecated alias for 'autonomous'.

autonomous_scope_allowlist.description: Dot-notation paths the actor MAY auto-edit when mode='autonomous'. Wildcards allowed (e.g., 'persona.task_modes.*'). Required when mode='autonomous'.

autonomous_scope_blocklist.description: Dot-notation paths always blocked, even when mode='autonomous'. Wildcards allowed. Recommended to always include identity.*, character.virtues.*.enforcement, self_regulation.*, values_and_drives.values.safety.*, governance.*, security.*.

approved_by.description: User id or org id that authorized the autonomous mode. Required when mode is 'autonomous'; optional for 'suggesting', where no spec edit applies without a person.

last_approval_at.description: Timestamp of the last human approval of the autonomous mode. Required when mode is 'autonomous'; optional for 'suggesting'.

approval_expires_at.description: Optional. The time after which the approval of autonomous mode lapses and the mode falls back to 'locked', so consent is renewed rather than left standing. The open engine does not read this field yet.

runtime.description: Runtime constraints declared by the author, for a host that monitors the persona. The model never sees them. The open engine validates this block and does not act on it.

min_consistency.description: Floor for a layer's consistency score; below it, a monitoring host reports the layer as regressed. Default 0.7 when omitted.

drift_alert_channels.description: Channel URIs where a monitoring host sends drift alerts (e.g. 'slack:#observability', 'webhook:https://...').

allowed_consumers.description: Who may open a runtime session against this persona. Defaults to all three when omitted.

compiled_prompt_cache_ttl_seconds.description: Hint, in seconds, for a compiler that caches compiled prompts keyed by (spec_hash, state_hash, context_hash). Default 300 when omitted.

evaluation.description: Batch evaluation suites the persona version must pass before it ships, as opposed to the per-answer assertions below.

required_suites.description: Named suites that must be present and passing for the version to count as shippable. The suites are defined by the host that runs them.

assertions.description: Behavioral checks a judge or evaluator runs against the persona's answers. Each one declares the layer it covers and how it is checked. They are never placed in the model's prompt. `personaxis validate` and `personaxis lint` check their shape; the open engine does not evaluate them during a run.

layer.description: One of the ten layers of personaxis.md, or 'cross_layer' for an assertion that spans several. 'reflexive_self_regulation' and 'values_drives' are the older names of self_regulation and values_and_drives, accepted so existing policies keep validating.

name.description: Human-readable label, cited in evaluation reports.

type.description: Evaluation strategy. 'regex' and 'llm_judge' are defined; 'semantic' and 'activation_projection' are reserved and evaluate as a no-op pass.

definition.description: Type-specific configuration, shaped by `type`: `regex` takes a pattern and the field it is matched against; `llm_judge` takes the rubric the judge is given; `semantic` and `activation_projection` are reserved and evaluate as a no-op pass.

severity.description: Weight of a violation: info 0.5, warn 1.0, block 2.0.

enabled.description: Defaults to true. Set false to retain the assertion in policy.yaml but skip evaluation.
